language.name: English
cli.description: Browse and restore previous versions of files from btrfs snapshots.
cli.option.lang: language for messages (for example en or ja); defaults to BTRFS_TIMELINE_LANG, then the system locale
error.no-backup-requires-force: --no-backup has to be given together with --force, because it throws away the backup that would be taken before overwriting
error.live-not-restorable: the current (live) file cannot be used as a restore source
error.version-missing: the file did not exist at version #{index}
error.not-in-snapshots: this file was not found in any snapshot
error.source-is-directory: restoring a whole directory is not supported yet, name a file instead: {path}
error.same-path: source and destination are the same: {path}
error.not-in-snapshot: this path did not exist in snapshot {id}: {path}
error.not-our-module: this was not installed by btrfs-timeline, refusing to remove it: {path}
error.outside-root: outside the directory this server is allowed to read: {path}
error.bad-request: the request could not be understood
error.cross-origin: refused: this request came from another site
error.auth-format: credentials must be given as "user:password", with neither part empty
error.read-only: the server is running read-only, so restoring is disabled
error.web-extra-missing: the web UI needs the optional dependency: install it with 'pipx install btrfs-timeline[web]' or 'pip install btrfs-timeline[web]'
history.command: list the versions of a path found in snapshots
history.option.omit-missing: omit periods where the path did not exist
restore.command: restore a previous version of a file
restore.option.index: version number as listed by "history" (default: the newest version found in snapshots)
restore.option.snapshot: restore the file as it was in this snapshot
restore.option.to: write here instead of next to the original file
restore.option.in-place: overwrite the current file (the current content is kept as a backup unless --no-backup is given)
restore.option.force: allow --no-backup, and let --to overwrite an existing file
restore.option.dry-run: report what would happen and change nothing
snapshots.command: list snapshots that cover a path
browse.command: list the contents of a directory
browse.option.snapshot: list the directory as it was in this snapshot
browse.option.no-hidden: hide entries whose name starts with a dot
diff.command: show what changed between two versions
diff.option.from: the older version number (default: the newest one in snapshots)
diff.option.to: the newer version number (default: the current file)
diff.binary: one of the versions is binary, so there is nothing to show
preview.command: show the contents of a previous version
preview.option.index: version number as listed by "history" (default: the newest version found in snapshots)
preview.option.limit: stop reading after this many bytes (default: {default})
preview.binary: that version is binary; use a redirect if you want the bytes
preview.truncated: (only the beginning is shown; raise --limit for more)
config.command: report what the user interfaces need to start up
device.command: add, remove or replace a device
device.argument.action: add, remove, replace, replace-status or replace-cancel
device.argument.device: the device to act on; for replace, the one being retired
device.argument.target: for replace, the device that will be overwritten
device.option.force: skip the check that refuses a device holding a filesystem
device.option.confirm: the exact device name, to confirm a dangerous operation without a terminal
operation.device-add-force: add {device} to {path}, overwriting whatever filesystem is on it
operation.device-remove: move everything off {device} and remove it from {path}; redundancy drops while this runs
operation.device-replace: replace {source} with {target} on {path}; everything currently on {target} is overwritten
operation.device-replace-cancel: stop the replace on {path}; the original device stays
error.token-mismatch: that did not match; nothing was run
devices.command: show the filesystems, their devices and how space is allocated
devices.option.usage: also ask btrfs how much of each allocation sits on each device (needs root for the detail)
operation.device-usage: show how much of each allocation sits on each device of {path}
operation.smart: ask {device} itself about its health: wear, reallocated sectors, hours
web.devices.spread: Every mount above is served by all {count} devices below. btrfs spreads chunks across them according to each allocation's profile; a mount does not live on one of them.
operation.device-stats: read the error counters of the devices under {path}
error.token-required: to run this, confirm the target by typing it exactly: {token}
error.confirmation-required: this command can lose data and has to be confirmed before it runs: {command}
cli.option.yes: do not ask before running; assume yes
cli.option.sudo: run the command through sudo when it needs root
error.needs-root: this needs root. Run it yourself, or add --sudo: {command}
error.needs-confirm: refusing to run without confirmation. Pass --confirm {token} when there is no terminal to ask at.
error.replace-needs-target: replace needs two devices: the one being retired and the one being overwritten
error.needs-yes: refusing to run without a confirmation. Pass --yes when there is no terminal to ask at.
scrub.command: check every block against its checksum, and repair what it can
scrub.argument.path: a path on the filesystem to scrub
balance.command: rewrite chunks to even out allocation across devices
balance.argument.action: status, start, cancel, pause or resume
balance.argument.path: a path on the filesystem to balance
balance.option.usage: only rewrite chunks less than N%% full; far lighter than a full balance
operation.scrub-start: read every block of {path} and repair what has a good copy elsewhere
operation.scrub-start-readonly: read every block of {path} and report damage without repairing it
operation.scrub-cancel: stop the scrub of {path}; progress is kept and can be resumed
operation.scrub-resume: carry on the scrub of {path} from where it stopped
operation.balance-start: rewrite every chunk of {path}; this reads and writes all of the data
operation.balance-start-usage: rewrite the chunks of {path} that are less than {usage}% full
operation.balance-cancel: stop the balance of {path}; chunks already moved stay where they are
operation.balance-pause: pause the balance of {path} so it can be resumed later
operation.balance-resume: carry on the balance of {path} from where it stopped
cockpit.command: install the Cockpit module, or remove it
cockpit.argument.action: install, uninstall, or path to print where it would go
cockpit.option.system: install for every user under /usr/share/cockpit (needs root)
cockpit.next-step: open Cockpit and look under Tools for "File history". No restart is needed.
serve.option.root: only allow reading below this directory
serve.option.auth: require HTTP basic authentication; BTRFS_TIMELINE_AUTH is also read
serve.option.allow-no-auth: allow listening on a non-loopback address without authentication (not recommended)
serve.option.debug: run in debug mode (verbose, auto-reload; never use when exposed)
serve.auth-required: refusing to listen on {host} without authentication: anyone who can reach it could read your files and overwrite them. Pass --auth USER:PASSWORD, or --allow-no-auth if you really mean it.
serve.no-auth-warning: WARNING: listening on {host} without authentication. Anyone who can reach it can read your files and restore over them.
web.path-placeholder: path to a file or directory
web.browser.title: Files
web.timeline.title: History
web.preview.title: Version #{index}
web.preview.binary: This version is binary, so it is not shown.
web.restore.title: Restore version #{index}?
web.restore.in-place: Overwrite the current file (a backup is kept)
web.restore.in-place-warning: The current content will be replaced. It is kept as the backup file shown above.
web.diff.identical: No change between these two versions.
web.diff.binary: One of the versions is binary, so there is nothing to show.
web.directory.hint: This is a directory. Pick a version to see what it held at that time.
web.elevate.title: Some of this needs root
web.elevate.cockpit: How much of each allocation sits on each device is not readable without root. Turn on administrative access — the button below, or the toggle in Cockpit's header — and it will appear. Everything else on this page, and the whole file history, works without it.
web.elevate.standalone: How much of each allocation sits on each device is not readable without root, and this server deliberately runs as you rather than as root. The Cockpit module can show it: Cockpit has a proper way to elevate with your own credentials, so nothing here has to invent one. Install it with 'btrfs-timeline cockpit install'. Otherwise, the commands below give the same answer in a terminal.
web.usage.title: What sits on each device
web.scrub.title: Scrub
web.command.read: What was run to read this
web.command.suggested: Commands you may want to run
web.command.why: These need root, and this server runs as you — so it will not run them. Run them in a terminal.
web.read-only: Read-only: restoring is disabled on this server.
